title: Have your coding agent work from reviewed written specs
summary: A developer built his open-source Agent Smith project with a spec-first agent workflow; he reports over 1,300 specs done and about 500,000 lines of code.
agent_role: Agents write a spec, a fresh agent reviews it against the code, then agents build, test and open a pull request. The human approves specs and merges.
outcome: Author reports 1,300+ specs completed, 1,190+ decision files and 650+ specs passed through the commit gate on Agent Smith.
what_they_did: A developer wrote a plugin where every change starts as a written plan, or spec. A fresh agent checks each plan against the real code. Then the agent builds it on its own branch, runs checks before committing, and opens a pull request. He built his Agent Smith project this way.
how_it_went: He reports over 1,300 specs done and about 500,000 lines of code since early 2026. Each spec leaves a file explaining choices made.
worth_knowing: A commit is blocked if any check fails, and the failure output goes back to the agent to fix.
prompt: Before writing any code for [feature], write a short plan file: the goal, the steps, facts from the code with file and line, and what done means. Then review the plan as a fresh reader and list anything wrong or missing. Show me the plan and review and wait for my approval. After I approve, build it on its own branch, run [test command], log non-obvious choices and why, and show me the result before opening a pull request.

curation.rationale: Open plugin with a clear workflow and counts from a real project built with it, though the post is largely a feature tour of the author's own tool.
